subject: Intermittent 429s and timeouts impacting MedAssist — urgent mitigation
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@medassist.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 429s + timeouts starting 09:05 PDT

Camila —

We're seeing a sudden spike of 429s and a handful of 504 timeouts across our integration starting at ~09:05 PDT. Usage pattern hasn't materially changed on our end (steady request fan-out from our ingestion pipeline). The app is experiencing cascading retries — users are seeing degraded flows.

Quick facts from our side:
- Region: us-west-2
- Error sample: 429 rate_limited (x-request-id: 7e8f3a) and occasional 504 gateway-timeout
- Start: 2027-10-02T09:05:12-07:00
- We've attached a small trace and aggregated client retries (api-trace-20271002.log)

Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side rate-limit change or if something changed in our project/org mapping? We need a mitigation plan and ETA for stabilization.

Thanks,
Liam
Director of Engineering
MedAssist

Attachment: api-trace-20271002.log (text log, 1.8MB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@medassist.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 429s + timeouts starting 09:05 PDT

Liam — thanks for the quick heads up and for the trace. We're pulling logs now and will triage immediately.

Proposed next steps:
1) 15-min triage call — joining now (Sean and Marissa on it).
2) If we confirm quota misrouting we'll apply an emergency project-level uplift for MedAssist to stop the retries from cascading.
3) We'll provide a short post-incident write-up with root cause and a durable fix ETA.

Stay on this thread; we'll update within 30 minutes.

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in 429s + timeouts starting 09:05 PDT

Folks — forwarding client trace. MedAssist is getting 429s and retries are cascading. On triage call we saw anomalous quota hits that look like org-level caps are being applied to a child project incorrectly (project-level throttles show 0 available tokens while org-level usage is low).

Attachments: api-trace-20271002.log

Can Marissa validate the quota mapping and Aditya help with a temporary uplift option we can apply while we patch? We should also consider an immediate fallback routing to a compatible model variant in another pool to reduce latency.

Camila

On Oct 2, 2027, Liam O'Neill wrote:
> Camila —
> We're seeing a sudden spike of 429s and a handful of 504 timeouts...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 429s + timeouts starting 09:05 PDT

Quick summary from infra/ops review:
- Root cause (probable): quota-tiering misassignment during a recent org tidy job (label sync) caused MedAssist's high-traffic project to inherit an org-default cap instead of its reserved project quota. The quota metadata shows project-tier: "standard" but effective_throttle_bucket: "org-default-low".
- Evidence: matching traces (x-request-id) and quota-lookup logs show the mapping flip at 2027-10-02T08:59:41-07:00 — right before the spike. Attached: quota-mappings-lookup.csv (sample rows) and filtered trace.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (what we can do in the next 30–90 minutes):
1) Emergency project-level uplift: temporarily bump MedAssist project token pool to the committed throughput (apply policy override) — ETA 8 minutes.
2) Short-term routing change: route MedAssist to the secondary dedicated pool in us-west-2 (compatible model variant) — ETA 20 minutes to flip and validate.
3) Apply a rollback for the label sync job that triggered misassignment and add a guard to prevent auto-assigning org-default-low to projects with reserved capacity.

Longer term: permanent fix in INF-3249 (quota service validation + stronger invariants), plus an audit of recent tidy jobs.

I'll prepare the uplift and routing change now.

—Marissa
Senior Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: quota-mappings-lookup.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief: MedAssist 429 surge — mitigation underway

Aditya — FYI / quick exec note:
- Impact: MedAssist production ingestion saw ~35% request 429s between 09:05–09:22 PDT; retries created a visible amplification to downstream systems.
- Action taken: Marissa initiated emergency uplift + routing to secondary pool. Both actions should remove the immediate throttling and stop the retry storm.
- Next steps: Confirm stabilization, then follow with postmortem and SLA-credit assessment.

We've attached the filtered traces and the quota mapping sample. I'll ping you if we need an exception for permanent quota increase or cross-region routing.

—Sean
Director, Customer Reliability

Attachments: api-trace-20271002.log (filtered), quota-mappings-lookup.csv

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@medassist.com>, procurement@medassist.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Mitigation applied — routing + temporary uplift (MedAssist)

Liam —

Update from the triage — we applied the temporary project-level uplift and toggled routing to the secondary us-west-2 pool at 10:14 PDT. Early metrics show 429 rate dropped to <1% and user-facing timeouts returned to baseline. We're still monitoring but the retry storm has subsided.

Next steps for us:
- We will revert the label sync change and harden the mapping validation (INF-3249).
- We'll provide a post-incident report including timelines, root cause, and a recommended durable quota increase (if you want it).
- If you'd like us to open an SLA credit request, we can coordinate with procurement — attaching a credit request template (SLA-credit-request-template.docx).

Apologies for the disruption. Let me know if you'd like a short technical review call.

Thanks for your patience — and thanks to Marissa and Sean for the fast response.

—Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-credit-request-template.docx

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@medassist.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, procurement@medassist.com
Date: 2027-10-04T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mitigation applied — routing + temporary uplift (MedAssist)

Camila / team —

Thanks for the fast mitigation and the write-up so far. We confirm the service has been stable since the uplift. Procurement has asked that we formalize an SLA credit request and also get a durable solution timeline for INF-3249 before renewal conversations.

Requested:
- Please send a short post-incident RCA (high level + timeline) and a target ETA for the durable fix.
- We will submit the SLA credit request this week; would appreciate Redwood's sign-off on a credit amount range so procurement can expedite.

Appreciate the team moving quickly.

Regards,
Liam
Director of Engineering, MedAssist
